text.p: Following are analysts' views of reports that Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp may be preparing a hostile takeover bid for rival Thyssen AG that would create a steel and engineering behemoth with annual sales of more than 63 billion marks.

"It's a wonderful idea, but impossible to see how they (Krupp) could finance it. Net of disposals, they would have to find about 10 billion marks. They would likely have to issue shares, and the market might not like that.
"It looks to me like a classic case where the victim gets bid up, but the value of the buyer gets called into question."

Sinclair sees synergies between the two companies in flat products and automotive pressings that would make the merger attractive, but the inevitable job cuts and need for approval from cartel authorities could pose additional obstacles.

"The two companies have combined about 195,000 employees, and some would have to go. If they got rid of five percent they could double their margins. They could easily get rid of 10-20,000, but the final number is anybody's guess.

"The wild cards are the SPD (Social Democrats) -- which is powerful in Dortmund and won't like it -- and it would also have to be referred to the European Commission, where it might not even be allowed."
